canonical_statement: The study assessed anti-PEG antibodies after SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and whether those antibodies could interfere with in-vitro measurement of the PEGylated drug pegfilgrastim.

The study used commercially available, fully de-identified human serum collected either at a single time point or serially after vaccination, grouped as mRNA-1273, BNT162b2, Ad26.COV2.S, or unvaccinated/pre-pandemic controls.

population.label: Commercial de-identified human serum grouped by SARS-CoV-2 vaccination status

canonical_statement: Anti-PEG IgG was measured with two commercial ELISAs: a poly-methoxy PEG-40K-BSA capture assay and a mono-methoxy PEG-20K-BSA capture assay.
The G-CSF ligand-binding assay used anti-G-CSF capture/detection antibodies, a 200–6000 pg/mL pegfilgrastim calibration curve, and a 2000 pg/mL pegfilgrastim serum spike.
The G-CSF-receptor cell-based assay used AML-193 cells, a 1000–60,000 pg/mL pegfilgrastim calibration curve, serum diluted 1:5, and anti-PEG antibody staining with flow-cytometric readout.
Longitudinal anti-poly-PEG IgG measurements were obtained from mRNA-1273, BNT162b2, and Ad26.COV2.S serum cohorts to evaluate response magnitude and persistence after vaccination.
PEG-2000-linked polystyrene beads were used to deplete anti-PEG IgG before repeating pegfilgrastim ligand-binding and cell-based assays.
A competitive saturation experiment tested three donor sera across increasing pegfilgrastim concentrations selected to bracket clinically relevant concentrations associated with 2-mg and 6-mg doses.

canonical_statement: Analytical runs used four-parameter logistic standard curves with standards required within ±20% of expected values and R² at least 0.990; group comparisons used one-way ANOVA with Tukey multiple comparisons and correlations used simple linear regression.

At the single-time-point assessment, median anti-poly-PEG IgG titers were 12,373 ng/mL after mRNA-1273, 6,158 after BNT162b2, 6,473 after Ad26.COV2.S, and 5,911 in controls; the mRNA-1273 group was significantly higher than the other groups.

canonical_statement: The study evaluated pegfilgrastim only; other PEGylated products differ in PEG structure, size, and product immunogenicity, so interference cannot be assumed to generalize quantitatively.
The study did not evaluate whether anti-PEG antibodies alter in-vivo pegfilgrastim clearance or clinical efficacy.
Anti-PEG antibody titer was not a sufficient stand-alone predictor of assay interference because some high-titer sera had little detection loss and some low/moderate-titer sera had reduced recovery.

The authors concluded that anti-PEG antibodies can interfere with in-vitro measurement of PEGylated drug concentrations and should be considered during preclinical and clinical development of PEGylated drugs, with new assays or approaches potentially needed for accurate assessment.
The study was funded entirely through internal U.S. Food and Drug Administration sources.
The authors declared no conflicts of interest.
